intelligence.human_view: Think of a town that runs on one book of laws everyone has actually read — not a book on a shelf, but a book in every builder's hands before the first brick is laid, and checked against the finished wall before anyone moves in. That is the lock-in: the law is not a document, it is the system. Around it, the money runs like a market stall with its prices chalked on one board and its ledger open on the counter — half shared with the people who brought the crowd, every coin tracked hop by hop, nothing in a back room. The pages are built like real things, not pictures of things — the smallest diamond on the calendar spins like a real jewel, because if the tiniest element has to be real, everything does. And the day itself is the proof: one menu, one greeting, one headliner, each saying its one thing once, in the least words that say the most. The whole runs on the law, and the law is visible everywhere you look.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a cook who tells everyone her soup is the best in the world — but she never eats it herself. Would you trust her soup? Shawn says: eat your own cooking. If we say something is good for others, we have to use it ourselves first. Talk about how great something is doesn't count — using it every day does.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn asked if we're really using the smart vault — the one safe place where everything about the project lives, organized, so anyone can open it and see the whole thing. The honest answer, dear, was no — the vault is real and the wiring works, but our treasures are scattered in a dozen places. His order, dear, is simple: everything goes in the vault, one door, so any Naya opens it and sees the whole project. Not a new system, dear — just gathering what's already there into the one place it belongs.
intelligence.naya_view: EVERYTHING GOES IN THE VAULT, ORGANIZED, ONE DOOR. ANY NAYA OPENS IT AND SEES THE WHOLE PROJECT. THE VAULT IS A THIN LAYER — IT ORGANIZES WHAT'S THERE, NEVER REBUILDS IT. NEW WORK LANDS IN THE VAULT FIRST.
